q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
I need to clarify what this question is asking. The question title says "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?" 

However, the research provided shows that **on May 20, 2026, NVIDIA already issued forward guidance for Q2 FY2027**, which predicts $91.0 billion ± 2% (range: $89.18B to $92.82B).

The question appears to be asking me to forecast what the *actual* forward guidance number will be when Q2 FY2027 earnings are released. Since we're currently on August 23, 2026, and the guidance was already issued on May 20, 2026, the forward guidance figure is already known: **$91.0 billion (±2%)**.

However, let me interpret this more charitably: perhaps the question is asking what the *actual midpoint* of their forward guidance will state when formally announced in the earnings release, if there's any difference from the May guidance. Or perhaps this is asking about what guidance they'll issue at that time that goes *beyond* Q2 FY2027.

Given the ambiguity and that the research explicitly states the guidance is $91.0 billion, I'll treat this as asking: "What will the numeric value of NVIDIA's forward guidance be for Q2 FY2027 revenue when formally announced?"

**(a) Time left until resolution:**
Q2 FY2027 would end around July 2026 (if NVIDIA follows standard quarters). However, given today is August 23, 2026, and guidance was issued May 20, 2026, the formal earnings release likely occurred in late August 2026. The question appears to have already resolved or is about to resolve imminently.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why:**
The most likely value is **$91.0 billion**, as this is the explicit guidance already issued on May 20, 2026. NVIDIA typically maintains its guidance unless circumstances force a change. The range stated was $91.0B ± 2% ($89.18B to $92.82B). Since this guidance has already been publicly stated, the midpoint of the forward guidance range is effectively locked at $91.0B.

**(c) What would push the value lower?**
- Unexpected supply chain disruptions
- Broader macroeconomic downturn reducing AI compute demand
- Increased competition eroding pricing power
- Regulatory restrictions on data center exports
- Significant miss in Q1 FY2027 results (though Q1 actually beat by ~$2B)

**(d) What would push the value higher?**
- Unexpectedly strong AI adoption and data center spending
- Market share gains from competitors
- Higher ASPs than anticipated
- Demand acceleration beyond current estimates
- Q1 significantly beat guidance by ~$2B, showing conservative guidance may persist

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values:**
From the research: Q1 FY2027 reported $81.6B against guidance of ~$79.6B, representing a ~$2B beat (slight upside). Q1 FY2027 saw year-ago revenue of $46.7B, with Q2 guidance of $91.0B representing 95% growth YoY.

**Analysis:**
The forward guidance of $91.0B has already been formally issued and is a matter of public record. Unless NVIDIA issues a revised guidance before the formal Q2 earnings release (which is unusual unless there's a material change), the answer should be $91.0 billion or very close to it within the ±2% range.

The range provided (99.5B to 115.5B) is notably above the stated guidance of $91.0B. This suggests either:
1. The question expects upside surprise (guidance raised at earnings)
2. The question is poorly calibrated to the actual stated guidance
3. There's a different interpretation I'm missing

Given that NVIDIA just issued explicit guidance of $91.0B ±2%, and companies rarely raise guidance significantly at earnings releases (more common to beat on actuals while maintaining guidance), I expect the formal guidance statement to be at or very near $91.0B.

The upper bound of the given range (115.5B) would represent a 27% increase from stated guidance—extremely unlikely. The lower bound (99.5B) is still ~9.4% above guidance, which would represent an upside revision.

Most probable: $91.0B guidance stands as stated.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, predicts $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). The midpoint of this range ($91.0 billion) implies a near-doubling of revenue compared to the year-ago quarter, which saw $46.7 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, exceeding its own guidance by approximately $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Gross margins are expected to be 74.9% (GAAP) and 75.0% (non-GAAP) for Q2 FY2027 [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).
